blocking_findings.finding: The tracer assigns a stabilizer role (0.25) to facial musculature. The demonstrated one-arm push-up and its stated anti-extension, anti-rotation, shoulder, elbow, scapular, and postural demands do not biomechanically support zygomaticus major as a movement stabilizer.
blocking_findings.suggested_correction: In a future revision, constrain stabilization tracing to muscles anatomically relevant to the stated joint and trunk/limb stabilization demands; exclude facial, ocular, laryngeal, and other unrelated muscles.

blocking_findings.finding: The tracer assigns a stabilizer role (0.25) to laryngeal musculature, an anatomically unrelated pattern that is not supported by the exercise instructions or frames. This is representative of the materially overbroad profile: 408 of 466 muscles are labeled stabilizers, including unrelated facial, ocular, pharyngeal, pelvic, and distal muscles.
blocking_findings.suggested_correction: In a future revision, repair the postural-stabilization mapping so it does not indiscriminately activate the broad anatomical catalog.

blocking_findings.finding: The unilateral one-hand-supported movement is traced with equal primary activation for both left and right triceps heads (and likewise for both sides of pectoralis major). A single repetition uses one working arm; the source does not support simultaneous bilateral primary upper-limb recruitment.
blocking_findings.suggested_correction: In a future revision, make primary-mover output conditional on the selected working side, or represent an unspecified-side exercise without labeling both sides as concurrently primary.

openai_reviewer.summary: The proposed exercise identity and main closed-chain horizontal-push mechanics are supported by the instructions and frames, but the resulting tracer profile is materially invalid: it labels an anatomically indiscriminate set of muscles as stabilizers and represents a unilateral push-up as bilateral primary upper-limb activation.
